sphere_commentary.overview:
The data suggest that all three series achieve modestly positive outcomes, with distinct consistency patterns reflecting their design intents.
• HEALING shows the highest response volume (n=574) and tightest score dispersion, indicating reliable entrainment across anxiety, crisis, and overstimulation states.
• THRIVING attains comparable mean scores (6.96) but with fewer responses and notable variability among HOLD protocols.
• TRANSFORMING records the lowest mean (6.59) and the greatest standard deviations, especially for ASCENT protocols, signaling possible mis‑alignment with low‑affect target states.
sphere_commentary.cross_series:
Across series, efficacy signals align with protocol architecture and intended affective targets.
• HEALING DESCENT protocols consistently yield steady scores (≈7.0) and fast settling times, supporting their nervous‑system regulation purpose.
• THRIVING HOLD protocols reach high peaks (up to 7.63) yet display uneven uptake, hinting at subgroup effects in focus and creative flow.
• TRANSFORMING’s ASCENT designs exhibit the widest spread and occasional low means (e.g., X‑MC‑L3), suggesting challenges in sustaining low‑affect entrainment.
sphere_commentary.anomalies:
Several protocols deviate markedly from model expectations or display data irregularities.
• H‑CR‑L1/L2/L3: AutoGluon predicts ~7.96 but observed means hover 6.35‑6.52, indicating a potential model‑data gap for crisis states.
• X‑MC‑L3: Mean 5.7 with high std (2.45) and possible bimodality, diverging from the predicted 7.54 for mind clarity.
• X‑ME‑L1: Predicted 8.23 versus observed 6.74, a sizable under‑performance despite strong model confidence.
• H‑OS‑L1: Strong observed mean (7.15) yet only 30 YouTube views, highlighting discoverability issues.
These anomalies suggest either population mismatches, protocol‑design mismatches, or data‑collection artifacts.
sphere_commentary.development_signals:
Targeted adjustments could improve under‑performing or mismatched protocols.
[CONVERGENT SIGNAL] • H‑OS‑L1 (n=95): high efficacy but low reach; consider boosting Adviser routing and creating an L2 variant with stronger onboarding cues.
[CONVERGENT SIGNAL] • X‑ME‑L1 (n=39): large AutoGluon‑observed gap; investigate a possible listener sub‑group split and pilot a tailored L2 version.
[CONVERGENT SIGNAL] • X‑MC‑L3 (n=10): low mean and high variance; redesign or retire this protocol pending deeper subgroup analysis.
[CONVERGENT SIGNAL] • H‑CR‑L1/L2 (n=43/33): model predicts higher efficacy; experiment with extending the hold phase or adjusting rhythmic pacing for crisis entrainment.
[CONVERGENT SIGNAL] • T‑FC‑L3 (n=35) shows strong outcomes with modest reach; allocate promotional resources to increase visibility.
sphere_commentary.embedding_analysis:
Embedding drift signals indicate evolving analytical framing across runs.
• CROSS‑RUN DRIFT: 18 protocols exhibit cosine similarity <0.70, suggesting notable shifts in interpretation or data instability.
• CROSS‑PROTOCOL SEMANTIC CLUSTERS: insufficient embeddings for reliable clustering; too few protocols with stable representations.
• Confidence note: embedding‑derived insights are currently low‑confidence due to sparse data and high drift.
